notes: Assumed persona: home cook with a personal collection, no sharing.

Map formatting is fully fixed: all 3 with_skill runs this iteration render as nested headings/bullets, versus iteration-1 where 2 of 3 with_skill runs produced a cramped wide table (the exact pattern users flagged as hard to read). The fix was a one-line change to SKILL.md step 3, not a prompt-engineering workaround.

Spec visibility is fixed: all 3 with_skill runs this iteration wrote a complete issues.md with full Gherkin text, versus iteration-1 where 1 of 3 with_skill runs (vague-recipe-idea) never saved the Gherkin anywhere reviewable, leaving a human reviewer with no way to see specs that had, in fact, been written and published.

Eval 2 now discriminates: the added 4th assertion (goes all the way to a sliced, specced, published skeleton rather than stopping at a map) passes 1/1 for with_skill and correctly fails 0/1 for without_skill on the identical prompt -- this closes the iteration-1 gap where both configs scored 3/3 and the eval measured nothing.

New gap found, not yet caught by any assertion: issue-expansion/with_skill left one of four journeys ("Manage tags") with zero representation in the walking skeleton. The run flagged this itself in its transcript as a deviation from "thin path through every journey" -- better transparency than iteration-1, where this kind of gap went unflagged -- but no written assertion actually checks per-journey skeleton coverage, only subset-ness. Worth adding next iteration.

Cross-run contamination from sharing one live test repo is reduced but not eliminated. Explicitly instructing baselines not to browse other issues stopped them from copying title/label conventions by reading issue content (unlike iteration-1). But one baseline still reused pre-existing labels via `gh label list` rather than inventing its own, and separately made an unrelated self-inflicted mistake (linked its story issues to the original source issue instead of its own new parent issue). True isolation would need a separate repo or clone per run.

without_skill's mean pass rate fell slightly from iteration-1 (59.5%) to iteration-2 (56.1%) while with_skill held at 100% both times, which is exactly what should happen when assertions get strictly harder (3 new checks added this iteration) rather than with_skill getting worse -- the growing delta (+0.40 -> +0.44) reflects a stricter bar, not regression.
